verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              कथं धर्मे स्थातुमिच्छन् राजा वर्तेत धार्मिकः। पृच्छामि त्वं कुरुश्रेष्ठ तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥१॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited an old discourse of what was recited by king Vicharakhu through pity for all creatures.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। गीतं दृष्टार्थतत्त्वेन वामदेवेन धीमता॥२॥
verses.english: Seeing the mangled body of a bull, and hearing the highly painful groans of the kine in a cow-killing sacrifice, and observing the cruel Brahmanas collected there for assisting at the ceremonies, that king said these words:Prosperity to all the kine in the world!-When the slaughter had begun, these

verses.sanskrit: राजा वसुमना नाम ज्ञानवान्धृतिमान् शुचिः। महर्षि परिपप्रच्छ वामदेवं तपस्विनम्॥३॥
verses.english: And the king further said,-Only those who transgress fixed limits, who are shorn of intelligence, who are atheists and sceptics, and who desire the acquisition of celebrity by sacrifices and religious rites, speak highly of the destruction of animals in sacrifices.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मार्थसहितैर्वाक्यैर्भगवन्ननुशाधि माम्। येन वृत्तेन वै तिष्ठन्न हीयेयं स्वधर्मतः॥४॥
verses.english: The pious Manu has spoken highly of harmlessness in all acts. Indeed, men kill animals in sacrifices, actuated only by the desire of fruit. an a

verses.sanskrit: तमब्रवीद्वामदेवस्तेजस्वी तपतां वरः। हेमवर्णं सुखासीनं ययातिमिव नाहुषम्॥५॥
verses.english: Hence, guided by authority one conversant (with the scriptures) should practise the true course of duty which is highly subtile. Harmlessness to all creatures is the highest of all duties.

verses.sanskrit: वासुदेव उवाच। धर्ममेवानुवर्तस्व न धर्माद्विद्यते परम्। धर्मे स्थिता हि राजानो जयन्ति पृथिवीमिमाम्॥६॥
verses.english: Living near inhabited place and practising rigid vows, and disregarding the fruits of Vedic acts, one should give up the life of house-holder, adopting that of Renunciation. Only they who are mean are actuated by the desire of fruit.

verses.sanskrit: अर्थसिद्धेः परं धर्मं मन्यते यो महीपतिः। वृद्ध्यां च कुरुते बुद्धिं स धर्मेण विराजते॥७॥
verses.english: Mentioning respectfully sacrifices and trees and sacrificial stakes, men do not eat tainted meat. This practice, however, is now worthy of praise.

verses.sanskrit: अधर्मदर्शी यो राजा बलादेव प्रवर्तते। क्षिप्रमेवापयातोऽस्मादुभौ प्रथममध्यमौ॥८॥
verses.english: Knavas have introduced wine, fish, honey, meat, alchohol, and preparations of rice and sesame seeds. The use of these is not sanctioned in the Vedas.

verses.sanskrit: असत्पापिष्ठसचिवो वध्यो लोकस्य धर्महा। सहैव परिवारेण क्षिप्रमेवावसीदति॥९॥
verses.english: The hankering after these originates from pride, error of judgement, and cupidity. The Brahmanas realise the presence of Vishnu in every sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit: अर्थानामननुष्ठाता कामचारी विकत्थनः। अपि सर्वां महीं लब्ध्वा क्षिप्रमेव विनश्यति॥१०॥
verses.english: His adoration, it has been laid down, should be made with sweet Payasa. (The leaves and flower of such trees as have been mentioned in the Vedas, whatever act is considered as worthy and whatever else is held as pure by persons of pure hearts and purified natures and those eminent for knowledge and holiness, are well worthy of being offered to the Supreme God and not unworthy of His acceptance.

verses.sanskrit: अथाददानः कल्याणमनसूयुर्जितेन्द्रियः। वर्धते मतिमान् राजा स्रोतोभिरिव सागरः॥११॥
verses.english: Yudhishthira said The body and all sorts of dangers and calamities continually fight with each other, How, therefore, will a person who is absolutely free from the desire of injuring and who on this account will not be able to act succeed in maintaining his body.

verses.sanskrit: न पूर्णोऽस्मीति मन्येत धर्मतः कामतोऽर्थतः। बुद्धितो मित्रतश्चापि सततं वसुधाधिपः॥१२॥
verses.english: Bhishma said One should, when able, acquire merit and act in such a way that his body may not languish and suffer pain, and that death may not come.

verses.sanskrit: एतेष्वेव हि सर्वेषु लोकयात्रा प्रतिष्ठिता। एतानि शृण्वँल्लभते यशः कीर्तिं श्रियं प्रजाः॥१३॥
verses.english: Upon these depends the word. By listening to this advice, a king acquires fame, great deeds, prosperity and subjects.

verses.sanskrit: एवं यो धर्मसंरम्भी धर्मार्थपरिचिन्तकः। अर्थान्समीक्ष्य भजते स ध्रुवं महदश्नुते॥१४॥
verses.english: Being virtuous that king, who tries to acquire virtue and wealth by such means, and who undertakes all his measures after thinking upon their objects, succeeds in acquiring great prosperity.

verses.sanskrit: अदाता ह्यनतिस्नेहो दण्डेनावर्तयन्प्रजाः। साहसप्रकृती राजा क्षिप्रमेव विनश्यति॥१५॥
verses.english: That king, who is illiberal, and shorn of affection, who oppresses his subjects by undue punishment, and who is rash in his acts, soon meets with destruction.

verses.sanskrit: अथ पापकृतं बुद्ध्या न च पश्यत्यबुद्धिमान्। अकीर्त्याऽभिसम युक्तो भूयो नरकमश्नुते॥१६॥
verses.english: That king, who is not intelligent, fails to see his own faults. Best with infamy here, he sinks into hell hereafter.

verses.sanskrit: अथ मानयितुर्दाम्नः श्लक्ष्णस्य वशवर्तिनः। व्यसनं स्वमिवोत्पन्नं विजिघांसन्ति मानवाः॥१७॥
verses.english: If the king honours them properly that deserve it, makes gifts, and recognises the value of sweet speeches by himself uttering them always, his subjects then remove the calamities that overtake him as if these had fallen upon themselves.

verses.sanskrit: यस्य नास्ति गुरुर्धर्मे न चान्यानपि पृच्छति। सुखतन्त्रोऽर्थलाभेषु न चिरं सुखमश्नुते॥१८॥
verses.english: The king, who has none to instruct him in the ways of righteousness and who never seeks advice from others, and who seeks to acquire wealth by means that caprice suggests, never enjoys happiness long.

verses.sanskrit: गुरुप्रधानो धर्मेषु स्वयमर्थानवेक्षिता। धर्मप्रधानो लाभेषु स चिरं सुखमश्नुते॥१९॥
verses.english: That king, on the other hand, who follows the advice of his preceptors in matters of virtue, who supervises the affairs of his kingdom himself, and who in all his acquisitions follows virtue, succeeds in enjoying happiness for a long time.
